audit.whatIsWrong: GNAR! is named on every line of the full layer, its cooldown is never given, and the condition on its stun — the single most useful fact in this matchup — appears nowhere in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Mega Gnar throws everything around him in a chosen direction, dealing damage and slowing them. Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.' Standing in open lane turns his ultimate into damage and a slow with no lockdown at all. It is 90s at rank 1. The other missing number is Hop at 22s at rank 1 — mini-Gnar's only exit from a Shield of Durand taunt, so a spent Hop is a free all-in.
audit.corrected: The wall condition and both cooldowns written into the tldr, winCon, trade lines, cooldown block, do's, don'ts, key interactions and the late text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart contradicts the prose on five of seven stages. It reads Skill, Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Gnar, Gnar — but spikes[0] is titled 'Gnar's window' at level 1, whys[2] says you lock down his hops at 3, whys[3] 'your taunt-and-knockup trade beats his ranged kite', whys[4] hands you the level-6 roam, whys[5] says 'your cooldowns and tanky-AP build hold up', and whys[6] calls the late game even.
audit.why: The prose describes Gnar winning level 1, an even level 2, and Galio owning 3 through the first item before it evens out — and the headline 53.33% agrees that Galio is slightly ahead overall.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Gnar / Skill / Galio / Galio / Galio / Galio / Skill in both layers with matching ratings, and diff moved from EVEN to FAV at 5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why calls Stormsurge/Riftmaker your spike on a stage the old chart gave Gnar, and phases[4].why ends with the boilerplate 'Reassess his ultimate too'.
audit.why: His spikes are every Rage bar fill, not a level — Rage Gene transforms him on the next ability at maximum Rage — plus level 6 and his first item. Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against Winds of War's 825, which is the whole reason level 1 is his.
audit.corrected: Stage lines rebuilt around Rage, the 1100-vs-825 range gap and Hop's 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The loading tip ends '- Anti-heal if he sustains.'
audit.why: Gnar has no healing anywhere in his kit, so Grievous Wounds does nothing here and the line wastes the one screen the player reads before the game.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the wall rule and the Rage-bar timing.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are your window. His boomerang and hops are AD and built to kite, but the W taunt locks him in place so the kite stops mattering the moment you land Justice Punch (E) to close — that taunt-into-knockup is your whole trade pattern. The real spike is 6: Hero's Entrance (R) means even if Gnar is freezing and chipping you, you channel out, drop the knockup-taunt onto a sidelane or river gank, and swing the map. Watch his Rage bar — if it is near full he transforms mid-trade and the mega wall-stun (R) flips your all-in, so force your trades while he is still mini and Rage is low.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are your window. The real spike is 6: Hero's Entrance (R) means even if Gnar is freezing and chipping you, you channel out, drop the knockup-taunt onto a sidelane or river gank, and swing the map. edits.before: By two items the duel evens back out: mega-Gnar's AD burst and his AoE wall-stun (R) punch straight through your shield, because Shield of Durand's damage reduction is only heavily amplified versus magic and almost none of Gnar's kit is magic damage. Your value here is not the 1v1 — it is using the W taunt and E knockup to peel and eat his mega-R for your team, then rotating with Hero's Entrance (R) to make plays elsewhere. Never facecheck a kiting Gnar with Rage banked; let your team collapse on him rather than chasing alone.
